PDB loaders iterate all topology residues despite claiming single/first-chain input. Multiple chains are concatenated and chain boundaries are treated as peptide bonds in flattened internal coordinates.

The advertised exact Cartesian log likelihood omits the Gaussian normalization constant for the harmonic bond prior and does not define the rigid-body six-DOF measure; absolute cross-protein/cross-length logP is therefore not established.
Validation samples are removed from training but never evaluated; limit_val_batches is zero and top checkpoints monitor training loss only.

Delivered Langevin defaults use non-GHMC dynamics with force clipping. Clipped forces are no longer gradients of the declared energy, so the default BAOAB path is biased even though the README recommends the exact GHMC configuration.

Dependencies are unpinned README commands with no pyproject/requirements/lock; the only smoke test omits the data parsing, cache, X/PAD, multichain, training, likelihood and Langevin contracts; README claims MIT but LICENSE is absent.

strengths: The heuristic scorer explicitly labels itself a crude, non-biophysical proxy.
The synthetic target is deterministic, split-seeded, and clearly separated from external Hugging Face datasets.
ESM scoring computes an explicit average masked-token pseudo-log-likelihood rather than presenting an opaque score.
README distinguishes synthetic demonstration metrics from a future real FLIP/SKEMPI split and calls for wet-lab experiments.
limitations: No target protein sequence, structure, complex, interface, docking, affinity assay, or wet-lab observation enters the default ranking; ESM2 naturalness and hydropathy do not establish target-specific binding or improved affinity.

The max-mutation and preserved-length constraints exist only in prompts; generated/evolved sequences are alphabetically filtered but are not validated against the seed, length, alphabet, mutation count, cysteine/framework integrity, or liability motifs.
The protein_binder preset names ESM as the scorer; a trained predictor is used only when separately configured, and its task/label semantics are not constrained beyond a generic scalar.
Default training uses a synthetic composition/motif target, so its RMSE/Spearman values demonstrate learning the synthetic rule, not protein fitness or binding generalization.

The generic Hugging Face loader infers sequence and target columns but does not define dataset version, split provenance, leakage controls, assay direction/units, replicate handling, or train/test homology partitioning.
The claimed resume implementation restores only metrics history and start_epoch; it does not restore model or optimizer state, so it is not a scientific continuation of the prior fit.
Static inspection indicates FSDP checkpoint collection is called only inside rank0(), while full-state-dict collection is a distributed collective; this can hang or fail and was not runtime-tested.

Elo ranking converts heterogeneous scorer differences through an uncalibrated base-10 logistic and stochastically blends a binary LLM decision; ratings are relative workflow artifacts, not calibrated scientific probabilities.

security_review.secret_scan: No committed private key, GitHub token, AWS access key, secret access key, API key, or password pattern found in tracked text. .env.example contains identifiers and empty/default settings only.

findings.finding: torch.load(model.pt) deserializes a user-selected checkpoint without a weights-only restriction; an untrusted checkpoint can execute pickle payloads.

WebSocket sessions have no authentication, origin authorization, concurrency quota, or server-side rounds bound. A remote client can trigger repeated Bedrock calls, model downloads/scoring, and persistent writes if the server is bound beyond its default 127.0.0.1.

Dependencies are lower-bound ranges rather than locked artifacts; Hugging Face models/datasets are selected by mutable names without revisions or integrity pins, expanding supply-chain and reproducibility risk.

The config loader accepts a filesystem path, and the WebSocket exposes that field without an allowlist. Pydantic limits interpreted fields, but an exposed server can probe/parse local YAML paths and alter resource parameters.

positive_controls: No shell/subprocess execution exists in the Python application path.
Frontend escapes raw markdown before introducing a small fixed HTML subset.
AWS credentials are delegated to boto3's normal credential chain rather than stored in source.

data_flows: Research goals, sequences, critiques, and other prompt context are sent to AWS Bedrock when the Bedrock provider is selected.

controls_and_gaps: No telemetry or bespoke upload path was found beyond configured Bedrock/Hugging Face access.
No retention limit, deletion workflow, encryption-at-rest control, redaction, consent gate, or PHI warning is implemented.
The web UI streams full agent event content to the connected client and has no user/session access control.
security_review.assessment: Do not submit patient, proprietary sequence, credential, or unpublished sensitive research content without a separately approved deployment and retention policy.

separate_provenance_risks: ESM2 weights, Hugging Face datasets, Bedrock APIs/models, papers, and scientific databases are external works/services whose licenses and terms are not conveyed by the repository MIT license.

change_summary.summary: Initial standalone Java 21 Quarkus MCP server exposing 30 natural-language tools over a remote Dnaerys-hosted 1000 Genomes Project GRCh38 variant store via gRPC, with HTTP/SSE/stdio transports, Docker packaging, protobuf schema, annotation filters, per-sample queries, inheritance-model queries, and pairwise kinship.

positive_signals: The protobuf explicitly documents GRCh38, 1-based inclusive coordinates, allele/genotype counters, incomplete-cluster flags, and that trio inheritance methods are naive filters over existing genotype calls rather than specialized calling pipelines.
Tool filters cover commonly useful 1000 Genomes, gnomAD, VEP, Sequence Ontology, ClinVar, AlphaMissense, zygosity, allele, and length concepts.
The repository caps requested list sizes in the Java client and distinguishes homozygous, heterozygous, and combined wrappers.

critical_findings.evidence: All 18 client operations catch Throwable. Counts return 0 on transport/runtime failure and invalid input; list operations return or append the literal JSON string '{}'; kinship returns ''. These are also used for legitimate empty/no-match responses.
critical_findings.impact: Agents cannot distinguish no variants/samples/relatedness from malformed inputs, backend outage, TLS failure, partial stream failure, parsing failure, or other runtime errors; false scientific negatives are expected.

critical_findings.evidence: Protobuf count, list, sample, kinship, and allele responses expose incomplete_cluster and often affected flags, node_id, and elapsed metadata; DnaerysClient extracts only count, alleles, samples, or one kinship degree.
critical_findings.impact: A result known by the backend to be incomplete can be presented as complete, corrupting counts, carrier searches, inheritance conclusions, and absence claims.

critical_findings.evidence: The protobuf describes de novo/dominant/recessive selection as naive logic entirely based on existing genotype calls and says no specialized de novo pipeline is used; MCP tool descriptions call them de novo/dominant/recessive variants without surfacing that limitation.
critical_findings.impact: Users may treat candidate filters as validated inheritance calls without genotype quality, read-level evidence, pedigree QC, phasing, mosaicism, callability, or confirmation.

critical_findings.evidence: Tools filter on VEP, ClinVar, gnomAD, and AlphaMissense but return compact Variant JSON without annotation records, source versions, dates, review status, transcripts, or provenance; the repository does not pin data snapshot versions.
critical_findings.impact: Clinical-significance and pathogenicity interpretations are not reproducible and cannot support reclassification claims.

critical_findings.evidence: Unknown enum tokens map to UNRECOGNIZED and are silently omitted; invalid max/min lengths reset to an unrestricted range; invalid coordinates/chromosomes collapse to empty sentinels.
critical_findings.impact: Typos can silently remove requested constraints or look like true absence rather than producing validation errors.

critical_findings.evidence: MAX_RETURNED_ITEMS is 100 in the client, while protobuf comments define skip and limit per backend node; stream responses are concatenated and completeness/order metadata is discarded.
critical_findings.impact: The advertised cap may not be global and stable pagination/completeness across cluster nodes is not established.

critical_findings.evidence: The backend returns sample pair, degree, and phi_bwf plus cluster metadata; the MCP client returns only the first degree enum string.
critical_findings.impact: No coefficient, threshold context, pair identity echo, common-locus support, or completeness status reaches the agent.

claim_risks: README examples repeatedly characterize the 1000 Genomes cohort as healthy and propose disease-variant reclassification or compensatory mechanisms. A population reference cohort is not evidence that every participant is disease-free, and allele frequency plus an in-silico score is insufficient for clinical reclassification.

README claims 138,044,724 variants, about 442 billion genotypes, and 3,202 samples, but this audit did not query the service and the client discards dataset timestamp/data-format/notes needed to freeze a result snapshot.
Sex-stratified sample enumeration uses backend cohort sex labels without documenting provenance, meaning, missingness, or ethical limits.

findings.evidence: src/main/resources/dnaerys.properties sets db.dnaerys.org:80 and ssl=false; GrpcChannel then uses InsecureChannelCredentials.
findings.impact: Queries, sample identifiers, genotype selections, and returned results can be observed or modified in transit; DNS/network attackers can forge scientific output.

findings.evidence: When ssl=true, GrpcChannel installs an X509TrustManager whose client/server checks are empty.

findings.claim: Information Gain/ReliefF supervised feature selection is fit once on the full training cohort before any cross-validation. Every downstream CV fold therefore receives features chosen using its held-out labels, causing selection leakage and optimistic performance.
findings.recommendation: Fit feature filtering/ranking inside each resampling fold or use a true nested pipeline; reserve a locked external set for final evaluation.

findings.claim: Forward/backward/top-k feature subsets are repeatedly selected by maximizing the same 10-fold CV score later reported as performance. This is adaptive multiple testing without outer CV, so reported CV metrics are not out-of-sample estimates.
findings.recommendation: Use nested CV with the entire model/feature/hyperparameter search confined to inner folds and report only outer-fold performance.

findings.claim: Best-model sorting explicitly recommends TEST_* and TRAIN_TEST_* metrics, and the quick start selects TRAIN_TEST_RH_MCC after merging the held-out third back with training. The validation/test set can therefore drive model selection and no longer provides an unbiased final estimate.
findings.recommendation: Prohibit test-derived selection metrics; keep an untouched final test set or external cohort and state that biomarker claims require prospective/external validation.

findings.claim: Some CV uses fixed seed 1 while short tests, bootstrap sampling, and train/test sampling use unseeded new Random(). No global seed is recorded, so identical configs need not reproduce selected signatures or performance.
findings.recommendation: Expose one recorded seed and derive deterministic sub-seeds for every split/search/bootstrap.

findings.claim: Caller-selected .model files are loaded through Weka SerializationHelper, i.e. Java object deserialization. A model from an untrusted source can execute gadget chains available in the large bundled classpath.
findings.recommendation: Treat model loading as privileged and allow only locally produced, integrity-pinned artifacts; prefer a non-executable model format or strict deserialization allowlist.

findings.claim: The repository vendors a large set of old Weka/plugin/Apache/JFree jars and builds an uber-JAR while explicitly stripping META-INF signatures. There is no lockfile, SBOM, per-jar checksum, vulnerability record, or complete third-party notices in the audit surface.
findings.recommendation: Rebuild from pinned authenticated dependencies, retain/verifiably replace signatures, generate SBOM/notices, and remove duplicate/outdated jars.

findings.claim: The tool is aimed at diagnosis/prognosis/treatment-response data and persists sample identifiers, feature names, predictions, detailed models and intermediate tables. It is local-only and has no discovered network uploader, but supplies no PHI/pseudonymization, retention, access-control, or model-membership privacy guidance.
findings.recommendation: Require pseudonymous IDs, controlled work directories, retention/deletion guidance, and a warning that serialized models/signatures can leak sensitive cohort information.

findings.claim: No test source tree or CI workflow is present. Committed benchmark datasets, generated result CSVs, binary Weka models and a bundled release JAR are examples/artifacts, not an automated regression suite for the 235-commit scientific workflow.
findings.recommendation: Add deterministic unit/contract tests and leakage-safe golden evaluations before any reuse.

findings: The repository implements transport, upload and output formatting; physical/chemical pose checks are delegated entirely to the unpinned PoseBusters dependency.
No committed benchmark compares wrapper results with an immutable PoseBusters version or paper examples.
CSV parsing counts only exact strings True and False; missing, malformed or changed upstream values are silently excluded from the denominator.
The subprocess return code is ignored; when stdout is nonempty, a failed or partial PoseBusters invocation can still be formatted as ordinary result rows while stderr is omitted from the response.

The advertised full MCP compliance is not supported by conventional MCP JSON-RPC initialize/tools/list/tools/call surfaces; the checked code exposes custom /mcp/context and /mcp/predict HTTP endpoints with a repository-defined schema.

Unauthenticated endpoints read whole uploaded PDB/SDF files into memory and run an external executable for up to 300 seconds without upload-size or concurrency bounds, enabling memory/CPU denial of service.
os.chdir is process-global inside an async request path; concurrent requests can race across temporary directories and cleanup.
MIME validation trusts filename extension and client content-type, including application/octet-stream and text/plain, rather than inspecting content.
Unhandled exceptions return full traceback and internal error text to clients.
requirements.txt uses broad minimum versions or no version, and the Docker build installs mutable dependencies including the executable backend.
